bull_bear.body:
- Third largest Indian manufacturer of magnet winding wires by production capacity and largest exporter by export revenue in Fiscal 2025 (CARE Report)
- Comprehensive, diversified product suite (standard + specialised wires, CTC) enabling cross-selling across multiple end-use industries
- Large, strategically located manufacturing facilities close to Jawaharlal Nehru Port, giving cost and logistics efficiencies
- In-house development team of engineers, designers and technicians for new product/process development and cost reduction
- High entry barriers via stringent pre-qualification approvals: PGCIL, NTPC, NPCIL and RDSO product approvals for HVDC/765kV EHV applications
- Long-standing relationships with a diversified OEM customer base, domestic and global, under the 'KSH' brand; awards from Toshiba T&D, GE Power Grid Solutions and BHEL
- Track record of financial performance and consistent growth (FY23-FY25 revenue CAGR 35.55%, EBITDA CAGR 56.70%, PAT CAGR 59.83%)
- Experienced promoters (Chairman with 40+ years in magnet winding wires) and senior management actively involved in operations
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — Top 10 customers contributed 52.54% of FY25 revenue from operations (53.97% in Q1 FY26; 58.99% in FY23); loss of or lower demand from key customers would materially hurt revenue
- Elevated and rising leverage — Net Debt/Equity rose from 0.59x (FY23) to 1.17x (FY25) and Net Debt/EBITDA to 2.85x; Rs 2,259.77 million of Net Proceeds is earmarked for borrowing repayment, making deleveraging IPO-dependent
- Thin EBITDA margins typical of a conversion business — EBITDA margin of only 6.35% in FY25 (4.75% FY23) leaves limited buffer against input-cost or pricing shocks
- Export dependence and geographic demand risk — Exports were 32.70% of FY25 revenue across 24 countries; top five export countries (USA, UAE, Kuwait, Romania, Saudi Arabia) alone were 24.34% of revenue
- Manufacturing concentration in Maharashtra — All four facilities (Taloja, two at Chakan, Supa) are in Maharashtra, exposing operations to regional disruptions
- Promoter-group breadth and related-party linkages — Twelve promoters (98.40% pre-Offer holding) with directorships across a large KSH group conglomerate; KSH Distriparks and KSH Infra Park 4 identified as Group Companies due to related-party transactions
- Reliance on commissioned industry data — Industry positioning claims rest on the CARE Report, commissioned and paid for by the Company, which the DRHP itself flags as subject to inherent risks

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward integration is a stated aim of the manufacturing expansion: IPO objects include new machinery for expansion at the Supa Facility, a rooftop solar power plant at Supa, and new machinery at Unit 2 (Chakan, Pune), intended to improve supply chain resilience, reduce raw material costs and ensure consistent availability of high-quality copper rods, a critical input for magnet wire production. Primary raw materials are copper and aluminium with enamel and paper as insulating materials, procured from a small supplier base (9-17 suppliers across periods) without long-term supplier agreements; top-10 suppliers account for 96.93%-98.91% of raw material cost. Manufacturing facilities are located close to Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Navi Mumbai) for logistics cost efficiency. Sales are largely make-to-order via purchase orders rather than long-term supply agreements, exposing the company to inventory/raw-material scheduling mismatches. Capex additions to plant and equipment were Rs 86.39 mn (FY23), Rs 258.32 mn (FY24), Rs 17.06 mn (FY25) and Rs 8.13 mn (Q1FY26), constituting 46.71%, 54.95%, 31.50% and 79.63% of total capital expenditure respectively.

overview.business_model: Manufactures and sells magnet winding wires — round enamelled copper/aluminium magnet winding wires, paper insulated rectangular copper/aluminium magnet winding wires, continuously transposed conductors, rectangular enamelled copper/aluminium magnet winding wires and bunched paper insulated copper magnet winding wires — from manufacturing units in and around Pune (Birdewadi/Chakan, Khalumbre and the Supa Facility) to manufacturers of capital goods such as transformers, motors, alternators and generators, selling both domestically and through exports (largest exporter of magnet winding wires from India by export revenues in Fiscal 2025). Revenue from operations was Rs 19,282.93 million in Fiscal 2025; the top 10 customers (including Al-Ahleia Switchgear Co., Bharat Bijlee Limited, CG Power and Industrial Solutions Limited, Emirates Transformer & Switchgear Limited, Georgia Transformer Corporation, Nidec Industrial Automation India Private Limited, Transformers & Rectifiers (India) Limited and Virginia Transformer Corporation) contributed 52.54% of Fiscal 2025 revenue from operations. Orders are typically placed on a make-to-order / specific purchase-order basis rather than long-term supply agreements.

genesis.founding_story: Incorporated in 1979 as Bhandary Metal Extrusion Private Limited; renamed KSH International Private Limited in 1996. Registered office shifted twice within Mumbai and then to Village Birdewadi, Chakan, Pune (jurisdiction moved from RoC Maharashtra at Mumbai to RoC Maharashtra at Pune pursuant to a special resolution of January 13, 2011, confirmed by regional director order dated August 16, 2011; certificate issued October 13, 2011). In February 2016 a Bombay High Court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement demerged the businesses carried out through investments in subsidiary/joint venture/associates (KSH Distriparks Private Limited, Kushal Motors and Electronics Private Limited and Waterloo Distributors Private Limited) into Waterloo Motors Private Limited, leaving the copper-conductor manufacturing business in the Company. Converted to a public limited company and renamed KSH International Limited in January 2025.
